rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so the pipeline tolerates this program and the binding constraints are satisfied; the lever now is obfuscation intensity. This sample is a hello-world-class Shootout binary: only 3 tiny functions (191 bytes of text total) and effectively zero meaningful runtime (one print), so runtime-cost sensitivity is dropped to near-irrelevant levels (0.20-0.40) and size cost is kept low-moderate since even multiplicative bloat on a 191-byte base stays trivial. SecurityGain and DiversityGain are pushed high across the board to maximize reverse-engineering resistance: FLA and BCF get the strongest weights (0.90) to restructure main's control flow and wrap it in opaque predicates, IBR (0.85) breaks basic-block locality, and ICALL (0.70/0.80) plus SPLIT and IGV add indirect-call and global-variable indirection for diversity, since with only three functions layering many weak transforms beats relying on any single one. CorrectnessRisk weights are held at 0.10-0.30 because the previous round showed no correctness fragility, but FLA retains the highest risk weight (0.30) as the transform most likely to perturb the static-init glue (_GLOBAL__sub_I_hello.cpp) if applied there. All seven passes are included so per-function feature matching can spread transforms across main, _start, and the init stub rather than concentrating on one.
